We used a publicly available TMS-EEG dataset from 20 healthy individuals. TMS was

Stronger TEPs were measured when pre-stimulus activity contained lower gamma power and higher

Our findings are consistent with the brain criticality framework highlighting how shifts in pre-
stimulus TEP dynamics influence cortical responsiveness. Reduced gamma power and fractal dimension were
associated with stronger TEP amplitudes, suggesting that states closer to order optimize responsive
conversely, higher gamma power and increased HFD, indicative of chaotic neuronal dynamics, dampened
perturbation responses. The opposite effect of alpha power highlights the frequency-specific nuances of criti
cality, where inhibitory mechanisms may fine-tune responsiveness.
